answer: In an agent marketplace, each seller of wharf schedules or raven sightings is a vertex in a trading graph and must lock a refundable stake for 30 days. Paid job opportunities are assigned in proportion to locked stake, rather than account count. Splitting one stake across a thousand fake agents earns no extra share of jobs. To capture more work, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital, paying its financing cost throughout the lock.
